title: Haplotype-resolved DiMeLo-seq maps centromeric chromatin in a complete diploid human genome.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.20214995 via API: one 236 KB zip of code (GitHub yxu405/HG002_epi_paper, MIT licence), no data tables. NCBI SRA esearch for PRJNA1451277 returned 0 hits and the ENA (European Nucleotide Archive) run report returned no runs on 2026-10-07. Europe PMC supplementary file listing timed out once (not retried).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That DiMeLo-seq (directed methylation with long-read sequencing) and ultra-long nanopore reads are in SRA PRJNA1451277; that Tables S1-S10 exist (contents unseen); the satellite annotations and CENP-A/H3K9me3/CpG methylation maps for one genome, HG002.

a1_downloadable.note: Only raw nanopore reads are deposited (SRA PRJNA1451277), which project rules forbid downloading, and the project was not yet findable in SRA or ENA. Zenodo holds code only; no processed CENP-A (centromere protein A) or methylation tracks found.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Any label (CENP-A occupancy, CDR (centromere dip region) calls) would have to be built by re-running basecalling, alignment and modified-base calling on raw reads; no label table was found.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequence inputs would come from the T2T-HG002 assembly (public), but the paired per-region signal is not deposited in processed form; not checked in files.

a4_units_stated.note: No processed table exists to check units.

a5_enough_rows.note: One donor genome, about 46 centromeres; per-bin rows could be many but are not independent. Count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Raw ultra-long nanopore reads, likely hundreds of GB (size not verified)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding labels from raw signal needs GPU basecalling and far more than 5 GB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No downloadable files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be physical measurements (antibody-directed adenine methylation on nanopore reads), though modified-base calls are themselves model outputs.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or AlphaGenome (DNA models) in principle

integration.partner_dataset: T2T-CHM13 and HPRC (Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) centromere annotations
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does alpha-satellite sequence predict where CENP-A sits across genomes? Not testable without processed tracks.

controls.positive_control: CENP-A enrichment inside hypomethylated CDRs (paper's main finding)

honest_claim_h3: At best: within one cell line's genome (HG002), predicts CENP-A occupancy along centromeres from local satellite sequence and methylation, which is not established to generalise to other people.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use centromere DNA sequence and DNA methylation to predict where the centromere-defining protein sits on each chromosome copy.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows from the 46 centromeres of one complete human genome with methylation per window; number of examples unknown.
plain_idea.predict: CENP-A protein occupancy per window, measured by antibody-directed methylation tagging on nanopore reads (DiMeLo-seq).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Centromere biologists would learn whether sequence alone sets centromere position, but one genome and raw-only data make this a resource-building project, not a modelling one.

ml_idea: Predict CENP-A occupancy along alpha-satellite arrays from sequence plus CpG methylation; blocked because only raw nanopore reads are deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; labels would need GPU basecalling and modified-base calling from raw nanopore reads.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether processed CENP-A/methylation bigWig or bedGraph tracks exist anywhere (GitHub repo, Tables S1-S10); none found.

verdict_reason: Fails A1/A2/A6: only raw nanopore reads (not yet indexed in SRA/ENA) and a code-only Zenodo record; labels would have to be rebuilt from raw signal, from a single genome.
